nodes.label: Join predicate

first_introduced_at.snippet: A join predicate compares column values from two tables to decide which rows match.

evidence.chunk_text: A join predicate compares column values from two tables to decide which rows match. An equality predicate can compare a foreign key with the referenced primary key. A matching row satisfies the predicate; a nonmatching row does not. Understanding a join predicate is prerequisite knowledge for interpreting inner joins and left outer joins.
evidence.snippet: A join predicate compares column values from two tables to decide which rows match.

evidence.chunk_text: An inner join returns only pairs of rows that satisfy its join predicate. Interpreting an inner join depends on understanding join predicates. evidence.snippet: An inner join returns only pairs of rows that satisfy its join predicate.

evidence.chunk_text: A left outer join retains every row of its left input. It uses the join predicate to find matching right rows. When a left row has no matching right row, right-side columns contain NULL. Interpreting a left outer join depends on understanding join predicates and NULL semantics. An inner join cannot represent all unmatched left rows.
evidence.snippet: A left outer join retains every row of its left input. It uses the join predicate to find matching right rows.
